protocol.title: A Digital Microfluidic Approach to Heterogeneous Immunoassays
protocol.platform: Digital microfluidics (DMF) on EWOD electrode array
protocol.objective: Heterogeneous sandwich immunoassay for Human IgG on a DMF device using surface-immobilized capture antibody, DMF-actuated incubation and wash steps, and fluorescence plate reader detection

layers: Bottom plate: patterned chromium electrodes on glass, 2 um parylene C + 130 nm Cytop hydrophobic coating
Top plate: unpatterned ITO-coated glass, 130 nm Cytop coating, pre-spotted with capture antibody

electrode_layout.platforms_per_device: 6 or 10 (wired in series for multiplexed parallel assays)

hydrophobic_coating.note: Cytop used in preference to Teflon-AF (50 nm standard); Teflon-AF too fragile for surface-based assays -- antibody printing caused tears preventing actuation. Cytop resists delamination during spot drying and rinsing.

actuation.application: manually to exposed contact pads on bottom plate surface
actuation.monitoring: CCD camera mated to stereomicroscope with fluorescence imaging (Olympus Canada)

detection.instrument: PheraStar multiwell plate reader (BMG Labtech, Durham NC)
detection.note: Device positioned on top of multiwell plate throughout assay; inserted into plate reader after all DMF steps complete

capture_antibody.post_spot_rinse: 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-127 in deionized water; allowed to dry before use
capture_antibody.note: Concentration selected to ensure surface saturation in spot area

detection_antibody.specificity: Fab-specific FITC-labeled anti-human IgG (raised in goat)
detection_antibody.label: FITC (fluorescein isothiocyanate)

surfactant_additive.name: Pluronic F-127
surfactant_additive.purpose: Prevents non-specific protein adsorption to device surfaces; facilitates droplet movement; eliminates need for BSA blocking step

buffer.note: All sample, antibody, and antigen solutions prepared in this buffer with Pluronic F-127

serum_matrix.note: 100-fold excess of bovine IgG over highest human IgG concentration; dilution required due to high protein content preventing DMF actuation

blocking_agent.name: BSA
blocking_agent.note: BSA blocking step eliminated on DMF device; Pluronic F-127 serves as functional replacement for non-specific binding prevention

steps.name: Capture antibody immobilization (pre-assembly)
steps.post_spot_rinse: 0.1% w/v Pluronic F-127 in deionized water
steps.notes: Fc-specific anti-human IgG physisorbed onto Cytop/ITO top plate by manual pipetting. Spots air-dried, rinsed, dried before device assembly. Top plate chosen over bottom plate to: (1) simplify fabrication and replacement, (2) avoid insulator damage from printing on bottom plate, (3) minimise interference with actuation electrode function. Extends bottom plate lifetime for multiple assay reuse.

steps.name: Device assembly and reservoir loading
steps.notes: Patterned bottom plate assembled with pre-spotted Cytop/ITO top plate separated by double-sided tape spacer. 1-uL aliquots of antigen sample and rinse buffer loaded into reservoirs before assembly.

steps.name: Sample incubation - antigen binding to capture spot
steps.operation: mix (10-pass cyclic DMF actuation across capture spot)
steps.notes: DMF actuation cycles 1-uL sample droplet back and forth across capture antibody spot 10 times (Fig. 2a/b). Active transport eliminates diffusion-limited kinetics: diffusion distances ~100x smaller than well plate. Dynamic system reduces non-specific adsorption relative to static incubation. 10 passes chosen to eliminate variance from fluid movement timing; 2 passes shown sufficient for binding saturation (Fig. 3) but 10 used for robustness.

steps.name: Sample removal
steps.operation: withdraw to reservoir + manual tissue removal
steps.notes: Sample droplet withdrawn to reservoir via DMF actuation. Waste droplet (containing unbound IgG and matrix proteins) manually removed from chip with laboratory tissue (Fig. 2b).

steps.name: First rinse - removal of non-specifically bound IgG
steps.operation: mix (2-pass rinse actuation across capture spot)
steps.notes: 1-uL rinse buffer droplet (10 mM phosphate pH 7.4 + 0.00625% Pluronic F-127) actuated across spot in 2 passes. Fig. 3 (inset) confirms non-specific adsorption to native surface and BSA spots is very low compared to specific binding; 2 passes sufficient for NSB removal without displacing specifically bound antigen. Rinse droplet removed to waste reservoir.

steps.name: Device reload for detection antibody
steps.notes: Cytop/ITO top plate replaced. Bottom plate reservoirs reloaded with 1-uL aliquots of FITC-Fab-specific anti-human IgG detection antibody and rinse buffer (Fig. 2c).

steps.name: Detection antibody incubation
steps.operation: mix (10-pass cyclic DMF actuation across assay spot)
steps.notes: FITC-Fab-specific anti-human IgG delivered to assay spot and cycled 10 times (Fig. 2c/d). Binding curve (Fig. 3) shows saturation after only 2 passes; spot captures antibody from fluid layer in direct contact with surface per pass. Pluronic in droplet does not strip previously bound antibody. Bulk droplet retains more antibody than bound by surface -- spot size and antigen density are limiting factors. Reynolds ~210; laminar flow.

steps.name: Detection antibody removal
steps.operation: withdraw to reservoir + manual tissue removal
steps.notes: Detection antibody droplet removed to waste reservoir and manually cleared with laboratory tissue (Fig. 2d).

steps.name: Final rinse - removal of unbound detection antibody
steps.operation: mix (2-pass final rinse actuation across assay spot)
steps.notes: 1-uL rinse buffer droplet cycled across spot in 2 passes to remove remaining unbound FITC-anti-IgG (Fig. 2e). Critical step: residual detection antibody in droplet would generate high background fluorescence at plate reader. Rinse droplet removed to waste reservoir (Fig. 2f).

steps.name: Fluorescence detection
steps.notes: Device (still on multiwell plate) inserted into PheraStar plate reader for FITC fluorescence readout from sandwich complex on top plate spot. After detection, Cytop/ITO top plate discarded; patterned bottom plate retained for re-use.

assay_performance.conventional_time_days: up to 2 (12 h antibody immobilization + 2-12 h BSA blocking + 1-2 h per binding step)
assay_performance.sample_volume_reduction: ~100-fold (1 uL DMF vs 100 uL well plate)
assay_performance.waste_volume_reduction: ~3 orders of magnitude (4 uL/DMF spot vs 3.5 mL/well)

serum_validation.matrix: bovine serum diluted 100x spiked with human IgG
serum_validation.interfering_species: bovine IgG at ~100 ug/mL (100-fold excess over highest human IgG)
serum_validation.result: linear standard curve obtained; low-concentration analyte detectable in complex matrix

binding_curve.rationale: 2 passes sufficient for binding saturation; 10 used to eliminate variance from fluid movement timing

non_specific_binding.mitigation: Pluronic F-127 in all solutions; no carrier oil (oil would form barrier preventing antibody-antigen binding at surface)

carrier_oil.note: Droplets surrounded by air only; carrier oil would form barrier between droplet and assay surface and could render assay ineffective

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.description: sample incubation, rinse 1, detection antibody incubation, rinse 2, fluorescence detection

bioscript.duration_units: All durations in minutes (m) or seconds (s); BioScript supports s and m only
bioscript.v2_fix: captureSpot variable never disposed; models persistent physical antibody spot on ITO top plate. All four mix operations reference captureSpot directly. Only liquid droplet variables (antigenBound, rinseStep1, sandwichComplex, rinseStep2) are disposed. Fixes use-after-dispose data-flow error present in v1.
